Hi Samira — thanks for the note and the kickoff deck.

I've attached our current master DPA (Redwood_DPA_v1.0.pdf) and a link to our published subprocessor registry for the most recent, environment-specific detail: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c_subprocessor_registry

Quick answers up front:
- Transfers: we rely on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for EU/UK transfers and also support adequacy-based transfers where applicable. We can include a transfer mechanism addendum if you have a preferred wording.
- E-sign: we use DocuSign by default and have an integration with AdobeSign as well (AdobeSign is supported, though some automated workflows are DocuSign-first). We can do AdobeSign if that makes procurement easier.
- Retention: default telemetry/usage logs are retained 90 days; aggregated metrics kept longer by default. We can discuss retention in the DPA annex if you have specific needs.

High-level subprocessor summary (excerpt):
- Amazon Web Services (compute & object storage) — hosting, backups (US/EU regions)
- Google Cloud Platform (regional workloads in APAC) — compute for specific customers
- Cloudflare — CDN and edge protection
- Sentry — error monitoring (anonymized traces where possible)
- Datadog — product telemetry and alerting
- Segment (or equivalent) — telemetry routing (used rarely; customers can opt out)

If you'd like, Ben can share a very narrow redline for section 3 (subprocessors) that clarifies our commitments around log handling. Laura from Legal Ops is cc'd and can coordinate the e-sign workflow.

Next steps: please confirm (1) whether AdobeSign is required, (2) any specific transfer mechanism language you need added, and (3) whether VertexPay requires us to declare any additional subprocessors for your procurement record.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Thanks — received the DPA and the redline. A few quick items:

1) AdobeSign: procurement requires AdobeSign for contract automation. We'll initiate the AdobeSign envelope from our side and route to laura.bennett@redwood.com as the final signer. Please confirm the exact person we should expect for signature (name/email).

2) Subprocessors: can you confirm whether Segment (or any telemetry router) materially processes raw attribution logs? The procurement/security team flagged attribution data specifically and needs confirmation that attribution-level logs are not sent to marketing/data vendors without a contractual promise.

3) Retention: 90-day default for telemetry is fine; we may ask for a 30-day option in the annex for certain event types — happy to mark that in our requested redline.

4) VSQ: I'll attach our standard VSQ export in the next message. Please let me know who on your security team we should expect to answer technical questions.

We'll create the AdobeSign envelope today and cc laura; please confirm the signatory and we'll route. If you prefer us to send the envelope to a generic contracts@redwood.com address, state that and we'll do so.

Regards,
Samira Khan
